newsitem.title: CHINA: Taiwan plane hijacked to China heads home.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan plane hijacked to China heads home.

text.p: A Taiwanese civilian aircraft hijacked to China on Monday took off from the southeastern Chinese city of Xiamen bound for Taiwan, an airport official said.
"The plane has left," the official said by telephone.
The Far East Air Transport Boeing 757 left the southeastern port city of Xiamen for Hong Kong en route to Taiwan to skirt Taipei's decades-old ban on direct air links with China.

A jobless Taiwan journalist, identified by Taiwan as Liu Shan-chung, had doused himself with gasoline and forced the airliner, carrying 150 passengers and six crew, to fly to China. It had landed safely in Xiamen and no injuries were reported.
Liu was still in custody and was being questioned by Chinese police, officials said. The hijacker alleged that he had faced political repression in Taiwan, airline executives said.
